what: The acceptance bar spike s1 (reco-alj) proposes for e3.1 (reco-zoz). These are the numbers an extractor has to hit for the module graph, the API surface and the architecture panes to be worth drawing; a language that misses one is not cut from the plan, it gets the fallback recorded in docs/concepts/structure-extraction.md and the reason the report gives.
how_thresholds_are_set: Recall is the bar that matters for a graph, because a missing edge is an invisible dependency; precision matters more for an export surface, because a wrong 'public' is a false promise in a breaking-change report. Each floor below is stated as (a) what a reviewer would notice and (b) what a grammar plus a language model can actually deliver, and `hard: true` means 'missing this makes the language unusable for e3.2..e3.7 at file granularity, so it goes to the fallback rather than to a caveat'.

throughput.comment: Parse-only throughput per core, release profile, over the corpus that represents the language: real files of that language when the host repository has any, otherwise the replica. The budgets this has to fit inside are ADR-004's `cold.graph.ms` and `warm.graph.marginal.ms`, paid per changed file, so 5 MiB/s clears them by two orders of magnitude; the floor is a canary against a pathological grammar, not a performance target. Missing it is a condition, never a no-go: cost is a feature-gate question (ADR-002 §6.5).

granularity.definitions: one row per named declaration at file top level or inside a type/module container, members included, function-local declarations excluded
granularity.exports: one row per top-level symbol nameable from outside the declaring unit, per the language's own access rules
granularity.imports: one row per (file, resolved file, symbol) dependency resolvable inside the repository

irreducible_blind_spots.what: Blind-spot categories the spike could not remove at any effort level, per language. A language whose run records one of these still passes, but the verdict is `go_with_conditions`: the category becomes a stated limitation of e3.1 rather than a rounding error. Anything not listed here is a bug in the extractor, not a property of the language.
